tasks.short: Choose and contract suppliers for employee services.

steps.what: Agree employee needs, service scope and spending limits.
Prepare a supplier request using requirements and standard terms.
Send the request to suitable suppliers and collect responses.
Compare proposal prices, coverage, service levels and exclusions.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and an agreed comparison field schema.
loop.output: Cited proposal fields, missing items and ambiguous terms.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate currencies, units and totals with rules; review ambiguous fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per proposal; unresolved fields return to the HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express coverage and exclusions in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Choose a preferred supplier against employee needs and service tradeoffs.
Negotiate price, service levels, liability and exit terms with the supplier.
Review contractual obligations, employee data handling and legal departures.
Approve the commercial commitment and any policy exceptions.
Sign the approved contract and obtain the supplier's signature.
Record service eligibility, contract obligations and renewal dates.

tasks.design: Configure request, approval and signature routing across {PROCUREMENT}, {DOCS} and {ESIGN}. A template generator prepares supplier requests, while a bounded extraction loop builds a cited proposal comparison and deterministic code checks prices and units. Approved structured terms populate the service catalogue and renewal schedule; people choose suppliers, negotiate and authorize commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Low purchasing frequency made bespoke integrations hard to justify. Inconsistent proposals also resisted simple field matching.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and signature configuration covers much of the workflow. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and template development effort; bounded extraction handles document variation.
tasks.still_hard: Service quality, employee acceptance and bargaining remain contextual. Supplier access, unusual terms and reliable price normalization still require effort.
tasks.human_edge: Understand which service failures employees can tolerate, test supplier credibility and negotiate workable remedies.
tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time assembling comparisons and chasing signatures, and more time reviewing service outcomes. No spending or contracting rights change automatically; quarterly reviews support recommendations on service scope and renewal.

reach.task: Assess employee-service value alongside the benefits package.
reach.learn: Benefit utilization, employee segmentation and total reward costs.

reach.task: Maintain employee-service eligibility and referral information.
reach.learn: Contract coverage, referral requirements and service exception handling.

evidence.claim: Request templates, approval routing and signature tracking can use deterministic configuration.
Pactum supplier negotiations at Walmart demonstrate a documented negotiation use case, but do not establish suitability for employee-service contracts.
GDPR requires lawful, limited and protected processing when suppliers receive employee personal data.
Employee consultation or consent requirements depend on national rules; Dutch works-council consent covers specified employment and staff-data arrangements.

assumptions: Time shares describe average internal effort across a contracting project, excluding supplier waiting time.
The company uses {PROCUREMENT}, {DOCS} and {ESIGN}, with some proposal comparison in {SPREADSHEET}.
Negotiation remains substantial, so meeting time exceeds the supplied means prior.
Build ranges cover one service category and available interfaces; consultation elapsed time may be longer.
Approved structured terms are captured during review, avoiding unreviewed extraction from signed contracts.
The solution supports procurement and does not score employees or applicants.
unknowns: Current systems, interface access and approval limits.
Contract volume, proposal formats and existing service catalogue quality.
Applicable national rules and representative consultation requirements.
Employee data shared with suppliers and the applicable GDPR legal basis.
Whether current contracts permit the proposed data processing.
research_questions: Can existing {PROCUREMENT} configuration cover requests and approvals without custom development?
Which comparison fields remain ambiguous across representative supplier proposals?
Would saved effort justify integration costs at the actual contracting frequency?
new_work: Review extracted proposal fields and resolve missing coverage or pricing units.
Maintain request templates, comparison fields and approval limits.
Handle failed signature routing and incomplete supplier responses.
Maintain service catalogue access and renewal notifications.

tasks.short: Arrange outplacement or relocation support for employees leaving the company.

steps.what: Retrieve the departure case, support policy and available services.
Check contractual support entitlement, deadlines and spending limits.
Discuss the employee's priorities, circumstances and preferred support.
Prepare a support plan with services, costs, contacts and deadlines.

loop.input: Minimal meeting notes, recorded preferences, approved entitlement and service catalogue entries.
loop.output: A support-plan draft using only available services and approved entitlements.
loop.check: Validate costs, dates and service identifiers with rules; HR checks preference fidelity and unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per case; unresolved content returns to the HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual priorities in free-text notes need faithful wording within a standard plan.

steps.what: Approve the support plan and any funding exceptions within delegated limits.
Confirm the employee's choice and send the agreed referral details.
Coordinate the first appointment using employee and provider availability.
Check whether support started and address concerns with the employee.
Record agreed actions, delivery status and case closure.

tasks.design: Create a restricted support case in {HCM} using policy and service records from {DOCS}; deterministic checks flag entitlement gaps for HR review. A bounded loop drafts the support plan, and configured flows in {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR} handle employee-approved referrals and appointment coordination. Human conversations guide support choices and resolve concerns, with structured follow-up feeding the case record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support crossed employee records, policy documents and external providers. Low case volume and individual circumstances made a dedicated workflow difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured case flows and reusable templates cover coordination. AI-assisted coding lowers integration effort, while a bounded drafting loop handles individual wording.
tasks.still_hard: Distress, disputed departures and relocation constraints need sensitive human handling. Provider availability and unusual contractual entitlements remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust during a difficult departure, recognize unspoken concerns and agree support the employee can use.
tasks.altitude: The HR manager spends less time locating entitlements and coordinating appointments, and more time on employee conversations and difficult exceptions. Existing approval limits remain; a 30-day follow-up creates a specific opportunity to recommend adjustments when support has not started.

reach.task: Identify short courses that support an employee's career transition.
reach.learn: Career-transition needs, course eligibility and limits on sharing personal information.

reach.task: Review disputed support entitlements during a departure.
reach.learn: Applicable agreements, national rules and respectful case documentation.

evidence.claim: Case records, entitlement checks and referral scheduling can largely use deterministic workflows.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; entitlement decisions retain meaningful human review.
AI Act Annex III identifies specified employment decision uses as high risk; applicability depends on the system's intended use.
A Danish study including HR occupations found modest average chatbot time savings, supporting cautious expectations rather than a guaranteed large gain.
GDPR legal basis, data minimization and retention requirements apply to employee records and provider disclosures.

assumptions: Time shares describe average internal effort per support case, excluding provider delivery and waiting time.
The termination decision is already made and falls outside this task.
Standard entitlements are available as structured rules; unusual terms route to human review.
The employee approves referral details; that approval does not establish the GDPR legal basis by itself.
Automated scheduling stays within recorded employee preferences and stops when no suitable slot exists.
Structured follow-up fields drive status updates; free-text notes do not automatically close a case.
Build ranges cover one support pathway; national consultation procedures can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Current entitlement rules, employment terms and exception approval limits.
Case volumes and the split between outplacement and relocation support.
Provider interfaces and willingness to exchange availability or delivery status.
Applicable national employment and consultation rules.
Lawful processing basis, retention periods and access restrictions.
Whether employees want a 30-day follow-up and how they prefer to be contacted.
research_questions: Can {HCM} case configuration support the workflow without a separate records app?
How many entitlement checks require interpretation of individual employment terms?
Can a structured preference form make the drafting loop unnecessary?
Which support-plan fields can providers receive without additional personal information?
new_work: Review plan drafts for unsupported promises and inaccurate preferences.
Resolve entitlement exceptions and failed provider referrals.
Maintain service availability, funding rules and scheduling preferences.
Check access permissions and apply record retention rules.
Offer and deliver the employee-chosen 30-day follow-up.

role.altitude: The HR manager shifts preparation and coordination into reusable workflows while retaining supplier choices, support approvals and sensitive conversations. Decision rights change only through explicit delegation; better records support more frequent service reviews and timely support adjustments.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Managers: connect employee-service spending with benefits value.
Training and Development Specialists: connect departure support with practical retraining.
Labor Relations Specialists: resolve disputed support entitlements under applicable agreements and national rules.
skills_to_grow: Structured entitlement rules and exception design.
Reviewing cited model outputs against source records.
GDPR data minimization and restricted case access.
role.ambitious_version: Run quarterly employee-service value reviews and offer an employee-chosen 30-day departure-support follow-up, using shared service records and human authority over commitments.
